Our book is the Dindorf Greek-Latin original of Aristophanes' eleven comedies. Multiple prior complete English translations exist, notably W. J. Hickie's (Bohn's Classical Library) made directly "from the revised text of Dindorf" — same source text — plus 18th-c. and 1912 versions. Far from first.

Our text is Calcidius's Latin Timaeus (to ~53c) in MS. Digby 23. Plato's Timaeus also has many prior English versions from the Greek (Jowett, Bury, Cornford). Prior English exists either way.

Our book IS the Henry A. Homes 1873 translation (Albany: Munsell) of Ghazali's Kimiya-yi Sa'adat, made from an-Nawali's Turkish abridgment. Documented as the earliest English rendering; Claud Field's English came later (1909/10). No English predates 1873.

Multi-work container: Porphyry Isagoge + Ammonius on Isagoge (Five Voices), Categories, and De Interpretatione bundled in one MS. First-translation claim ill-defined (rule 5). Also moot: each component has prior English translations (Warren/Barnes; Cohen-Matthews; Blank; Bloomsbury).

Helen Rodnite Lemay's 'Women's Secrets: A Translation of Pseudo-Albertus Magnus' De Secretis Mulierum with Commentaries' (SUNY Press, 1992) is a complete published English translation of this exact work, held by WorldCat/IA/Wellcome and reviewed in Isis. Prior complete English exists.

Thomas Newton's 'A Notable Historie of the Saracens' (London, 1575) is a complete English translation of Curione's Sarracenicae historiae, explicitly 'Drawn out of Augustine Curio'. Catalogued in EEBO-TCP, Bodleian OTA, NLA. A prior English translation predates ours by centuries.

Aquinas's De ente et essentia is among his most-translated works. Multiple complete English translations long predate our Latin scan: C.C. Riedl (1934, Toronto), G.G. Leckie (1937), A. Maurer (1949/1968), J. Bobik (1965), R. McInerny. Prior English clearly exists.

Our book IS the Vasu translation of the 17th-c. Sanskrit Hatha Yoga text Gheranda Samhita. Wikipedia and library catalogs (IA/Wellcome/HathiTrust) confirm Vasu's translation (1895, Bombay; repr. 1914 Panini Office) is "the earliest translation of the text into English." No prior English version exists; later ones (Mallinson 2004) postdate it.

sources_checked: Google Books / Amazon (Ancient Commentators on Aristotle series)
reason: Our item is Vatican Barb. gr. 591, a 12th-c. Greek manuscript whose primary text is Philoponus' commentary on Aristotle Physics Bk II-III (Vitelli 322-391). A.R. Lacey's complete modern English translation 'Philoponus: On Aristotle Physics 2' (Duckworth/Cornell, 1993, Sorabji series) predates ours; Book 3 also in series. Prior English of the named work exists.

Our record is Tersteegen's German compilation (1784-86, 1021pp fully translated). Scholarship on his small, well-studied English footprint says only hymns/letters/a biography reached English; "the bulk still awaits translation." No English edition of this collection found. Individual saints' lives are distinct source works, not translations of Tersteegen's German collection.

Eunapius, Lives of the Philosophers and Sophists has a complete modern English translation by Wilmer Cave Wright (Loeb Classical Library 134, 1921/1922), still in print and on Loeb/HathiTrust/tertullian.org. Our book is the source-language original of this same work.

Niccolò Liburnio's 'Le occorrenze humane' (Aldine, 1546) is an Italian humanist work (catalog 'Latin' is an error). All sources show only the 1546 Italian original plus a 1970 Italian reprint; no English translation, complete or partial, exists. Author is essentially untranslated in English.

Our book is the Latin Corpus Hermeticum (Ficino's Pimander). Abundant prior English translations exist: John Everard's complete "Divine Pymander" (1650, made from the Latin/Ficino tradition = same source language), then Mead (1906), Scott (1924), Copenhaver (1992). Not a first translation.

Aquinas's De ente et essentia (On Being and Essence) is among the most-translated medieval texts. Multiple complete modern English translations long predate us: Riedl 1937, Maurer 1949, Bobik 1965, plus Miller/Kenny online. Our item is the 1489 Latin edition w/ Gerardus de Monte's commentary, but the core work has abundant prior English.

Volume's bulk is Lactantius' Divine Institutes (Bks I-VII) + Epitome (pp.61-480), a Latin work with long-established complete English translations: Fletcher (Ante-Nicene Christian Library 1871; ANF VII 1886, based on Migne), McDonald (1964), Bowen/Garnsey (2003). Same work, same source language, prior complete English. Not a first.

Leontiev's 1875 "Византизм и славянство" (Byzantinism and Slavdom) was published in a complete English translation by K. Benois, Taxiarch Press, 2020 (217 pp., ISBN 9798692775023), explicitly the first English translation. Same work as our Russian original; prior exists.

sources_checked: UC Press / Unschuld Ben Cao Gang Mu Vol IX
reason: Our book is juan/chapter 52 (人部 Human Substances) of Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu (1596). Prior complete English translations exist and cover this exact chapter: Unschuld, Ben Cao Gang Mu Vol IX (UC Press), explicitly translates chs 47-52; also Luo Xiwen full translation (FLP 2003). Same text, prior English exists.

Our German Tractatus de Medicina Universali (1662) has all 154 pages translated. No published English translation locatable in Google Books, HathiTrust, OpenLibrary, WorldCat, or McLean's catalog. McLean's English "Metamorphosis of the Planets" is a DIFFERENT Monte-Snyders work; the 1666 Latin Commentatio and Newton's "Key" are not translations of this text.

Exact work = ETCSL composition 2.8.2.6 'A hymn/prayer to Inana for Ḫammu-rābi (F)'. Full prior English translations exist: Å.W. Sjöberg, 'Prayers for King Hammurabi' (1972) and the ETCSL online translation (tr2826.htm). Same Sumerian text; our quotes match ETCSL diction.

Boccaccio's Decameron has a famous, centuries-old English tradition: the near-complete 1620 translation (Isaac Jaggard, attrib. John Florio), reprinted 1625/1634/1657/1684, plus earlier partial tale translations from the 1500s. Many later complete translations exist. Decisively not the first.

Our book is the 1482 Latin Cosmographia edition of Ptolemy's Geography (complete 8 books). Prior complete English translation exists: Edward L. Stevenson (NYPL, 1932); Berggren & Jones (Princeton, 2000) translated the theoretical chapters. Same work, different edition. Not the first English translation.

sources_checked: websearch:gcod kyi zab don / Drametse / EAP105
websearch:Harding Heart Essence Profound Meaning Tibetan title/author
reason: Composite Drametse (Bhutan) EAP105 manuscript: 6 distinct works incl. the canonical Medicine Buddha Aspiration Sutra (pp.32-103) plus local Chöd/purification texts — a multi-work container, so a single first-English claim is ill-defined. Harding's "Heart Essence of Profound Meaning" (Wisdom 2025) is Jamyang Gönpo's canonical Chöd root, a related but distinct work.

sources_checked: scholarship on Ebers translations (Bryan 1930, Ebbell 1937, von Klein)
reason: Bolton's 1884 work is an ORIGINAL English essay describing the Papyrus Ebers (repr. Weekly Drug News), not an Egyptian text we translated nor a translation of the papyrus itself. Opening lines are English prose. "language: Egyptian" is a metadata error. No first-English-translation claim exists; full-papyrus translations (Bryan, Ebbell) are a different work.

Our book IS ETCSL 2.4.5.3. The Oxford ETCSL published a complete English translation of this exact text (tr2453.htm) on 18.ii.2000, freely online. Same catalog number = same work. A prior complete English translation predates ours.

This is the "mDo sde Pa" volume of the Neyphug Kanjur — a 106-vol manuscript copy of the entire Tibetan Buddhist canon. It is a scripture-manuscript copy AND a multi-work container bundling canonical sutras (Lankavatara, Ashtasahasrika/Shatasahasrika Prajnaparamita, Samadhiraja, Manjushri-nama-samgiti), all long since translated. No coherent first-English claim at volume level.

Hierocles' Commentary on the Golden Verses has long-standing prior English translations: John Hall direct from Greek (1657, EEBO), Rowe from Dacier's French (1707), and a 1756 ed. The companion Hermetic Asclepius is also heavily translated. Prior English exists well before ours.

Prior complete English translation exists: 'The Most Secret Mysteries of the High Degrees of Masonry Unveiled, or the True Rose-Croix,' trans/ed. Arturo de Hoyos & S. Brent Morris from the same 1766 French first edition (Scottish Rite Research Society 2011; Westphalia Press 2024). Same work, same source.

sources_checked: Google Books / AbeBooks (1792 first English ed., J. Johnson)
reason: Volney's Les Ruines (1791) was translated into English in 1792 as 'The Ruins, or, A Survey of the Revolutions of Empires' (London, J. Johnson), with a later famous Jefferson/Barlow version. Prior complete English translation of this exact work clearly exists.

sources_checked: Wikipedia (Order of the Golden and Rosy Cross)
reason: German GRC order's internal correspondence + admission statutes (35 articles + oath), a Kloss-collection MS attrib. von Röpert, c.1780. No English translation of this specific document found; only German editions and unrelated GRC docs are in English. Coherent prose, fully translated by us (15/15 pp).

Joseph A. Munitiz published a complete English translation, 'Nikephoros Blemmydes: A Partial Account' (Spicilegium Sacrum Lovaniense, Louvain, 1988), of Blemmydes' autobiography (Curriculum Vitae/Autobiographia). Our text is the Heisenberg Greek edition of the same work — prior English exists.

Robert W. Thomson's "Agathangelos: History of the Armenians" (SUNY Press, 1976; repr. 2010) is explicitly the first English translation, made directly from Classical Armenian — same work, same source language as our text. Prior complete English exists.

1523 Latin multi-work container: bundles De Natura Deorum, De Divinatione, De Fato, Somnium Scipionis, De Legibus, Plato's Timaeus, and Q. Cicero's De Petitione Consulatus. No single coherent first-English claim; each component has English translations (Loeb 1923-33 and earlier).

Gutenberg Bible = the Latin Vulgate, canonical scripture. A "first English translation" claim is ill-defined: the Vulgate has innumerable English translations (Douay-Rheims 1582/1610 directly from it, plus KJV, Wycliffe, etc.). Scripture-copy carve-out applies.

Our text is Chartier's Quadrilogue invectif (French original, 1464 MS copy). Two independent Middle English translations (R and U) were made in the 1470s-80s, survive in 5 MSS, and were edited by M. Blayney for EETS (1974/1980). A prior English translation of this exact work exists.

Herzen's "From the Other Shore" (S togo berega) has a well-documented complete English translation by Moura Budberg, 1956, reprinted by Oxford UP with an Isaiah Berlin introduction (1979). Prior complete English exists; our Russian text is not the first English translation.

Our book = Mornay's own collected letters/discourses 1600-1623 (1652 Elzevier French vol), fully translated. The only English version (Crump 1926, 'A Huguenot Family') translates Charlotte Arbaleste's biographical memoir of him to 1605 — a distinct work, different author/scope. No prior English of this letters collection.

Meibom's 1652 ed. is a multi-work container bundling 7-8 distinct ancient Greek treatises (Aristoxenus, Euclid, Nicomachus, Alypius, Gaudentius, Bacchius, Aristides Quintilianus +Martianus). Ill-defined first-English claim; constituents independently translated (Mathiesen 1983, Barker 1989, Macran 1902).

Our book is Barozzi's 1572 Latin edition of the two 10th-c. Byzantine treatises by "Heron of Byzantium" (Parangelmata Poliorcetica = de machinis bellicis; Geodesia). Denis F. Sullivan, Siegecraft (Dumbarton Oaks, 2000) is a complete modern English translation of both works. Prior English exists.

sources_checked: Bendt Alster, Proverbs of Ancient Sumer (1997)
reason: Sumerian Proverb Collection 9 has prior complete English translations: ETCSL 6.1.09 (full English translation, pub. 2003, Oxford) and Bendt Alster's Proverbs of Ancient Sumer (CDL Press, 1997). Same numbered work, same source language; our quotes even use ETCSL/Alster numbering.

Bolzanio's Institutiones Graecae grammatices (Latin Greek-grammar textbook, Aldus 1497/98), our 1557 Paolo Manuzio corrected edition. All known editions are Latin/Greek; no English translation found in WorldCat, CERL/ISTC, Bodleian, IA, Google Books, or scholarship. Valid first candidate.

Prior English translation exists: Octavo 2002 ed. 'On the Transportation of the Vatican Obelisk' (ISBN 9781891788246), Italian text translated by David Sullivan, commentary by Ingrid Rowland; corroborated by Drawing Matter. A 1974 Madrid Spanish/English bilingual ed. is also cited. Same work as our 1590 Italian original.

Work is Hero of Alexandria's Belopoeica (catapult construction). E. W. Marsden, Greek and Roman Artillery: Technical Treatises (Oxford/Clarendon, 1971) gives a complete English translation with facing Greek + notes. Our item is the Diels/Schramm 1918 Greek-German edition of the same work — prior complete modern English exists.

Obscure French Masonic Kadosh-degree ritual manuscript (Kloss Collection, Sudermania/Swedish-rite tradition). No English edition of THIS specific ritual text found anywhere. General "Knight Kadosh" English works (Pike etc.) are distinct rituals, not this text. We hold the French original w/ 18/21 pp translated.

Our German text is itself a 1733 translation of Defoe's 'The Political History of the Devil' (1726), originally written in English (ch.1 = 'Translation of the English Preface'). A non-English translation of an English original has no coherent first-English claim; the English IS the original.

Our text is a Meketre archive letter (Senwosret I, TT 280). T.G.H. James, The Hekanakhte Papers and Other Early Middle Kingdom Documents (Met Museum, 1962) has a dedicated 'Meketre documents' section publishing these letters with English translation/commentary. Prior complete modern English exists.

sources_checked: Wikipedia (French Rite, High Masonic degrees, Orders of Wisdom)
reason: French 17th-degree Masonic ritual manuscript (Kloss Collection, BPH, ~1800, anon, 7pp). An individual archival high-degree ritual, not a published work; searches found only generic 'Vénérable Maître' material and unrelated craft rituals — no English edition of this specific text. We hold it fully translated. Catalog-blind identity keeps confidence low.

Bonnet's Traite d'insectologie (1745, French; famous parthenogenesis/aphid work) was translated only into German (Goeze, 1773). All catalogs/scholarship cite the French original; English exists only for OTHER Bonnet works (Palingenesie, Contemplation). 1836 Compendium = different work. No prior English located.

L'Homme de desir / The Man of Desire has prior published English translations: an A.E. Waite-associated edition ("Louis Claude de St. Martin's Man of Desire") and Felix Mupidia Lonji's complete English translation (2017). Same work, prior English exists.

"The Siamese Tales" (Brewer, London 1796) is an ORIGINAL English work. Its "Translated from the Siamese" title page is an 18th-c. Orientalist pseudotranslation device; no Thai source exists (Brewer authored the fables, pub. in European Magazine). No coherent first-English-translation claim. Our 'Thai' language tag is erroneous.

1582 Latin imperial baronial diploma for Rudolf von Salis (Salis-Marschlins, Rudolf II). Event is documented but no English translation of its text exists in searched sources. Coherent translatable legal/heraldic prose; we hold the Latin original, 9/10 pages translated.

von Jan's Musici Scriptores Graeci (Teubner 1895) is a multi-author critical ANTHOLOGY of distinct Greek music treatises (Euclid Sectio Canonis, Cleonides, Nicomachus, Bacchius, Gaudentius, Alypius, Aristotle excerpts). A single first-English claim is ill-defined; constituents already translated (Barker, Greek Musical Writings, CUP 1984/89).

"mDo sde Ga" is one volume of the 108-vol Neyphug Monastery Kanjur — a manuscript copy of canonical Tibetan scripture. The General Sutra section holds ~266 distinct sutras across many volumes; one volume bundles multiple separate texts. No coherent single first-English claim: scripture-manuscript + multi-work container.

Vol 16 of Huygens' Oeuvres completes is an opera-omnia container (multiple Latin treatises + French editorial apparatus); first-English claim is ill-defined. Also moot: core works have prior English—De Vi Centrifuga (Mahoney, from this very vol XVI) and De Motu ex Percussione (Drake).

Codex Borgia is a purely pictorial pre-Columbian divinatory screenfold — iconographic/mantic imagery, no alphabetic Nahuatl prose or phonetic glyphic text (only a single later Italian gloss). No translatable source prose exists, so a first-English-translation claim is ill-defined; the cataloged "Nahuatl text" is a misattribution. Visual art -> not_applicable.

Each constituent Cicero work has abundant prior English translations: De Senectute/De Amicitia printed in English by Caxton 1481 (Scrope/Tiptoft); De Officiis by Whittinton 1534 and Grimald 1556; modern complete Loeb versions (Miller, Falconer). Same works, different edition. Not first.

Calvin's Latin Praelectiones in Jeremiae et Lamentationes (Geneva 1563) was fully translated into English by Rev. John Owen for the Calvin Translation Society (Edinburgh, c.1850, 5 vols), widely available on CCEL/sacred-texts. Same work, complete prior English translation. Not first.

Our book is a 1493 Latin incunable of Seneca's Tragedies. The work has a centuries-old English translation history: individual plays from 1550s-60s (Heywood, etc.) and the complete 'Seneca His Tenne Tragedies' (ed. Newton, 1581), plus modern Loeb editions. Not a first translation.

Our book is Erasmus's full Adagia (chiliades, 4151 adages). A prior complete English translation exists: Univ. of Toronto Press Collected Works of Erasmus, Adages vols 30-36 (Mynors/Phillips/Grant, from 1982), explicitly "first complete translation." Also a partial 1621 EEBO selection of 500 proverbs.

Exact title matches EAP105-1-3-38, an endangered Drametse Monastery (Bhutan) manuscript: a Sangye Lingpa Prajnaparamita terma. Lotsawa House has only one unrelated Sangye Lingpa text (Mandarava's Prayer). No prior English translation of this specific text found anywhere. We hold 200/202 pages translated.

Durkheim's Règles (1895) was first translated into English as 'The Rules of Sociological Method' by Solovay & Mueller (Univ. Chicago Press, 1938), with a later complete translation by W.D. Halls/ed. Lukes (1982). Same work, same source language (French). Prior complete English exists.

Paul of Middelburg's 1492 Latin Invectiva against Lichtenberger is engaged in scholarship only via Latin text + English paraphrase/summary (Vanden Broecke, Warburg); no full English translation found in Google Books, IA, HathiTrust, or OpenLibrary. Distinct from his Paulina/Prognosticatio and from Lichtenberger's Prognosticatio (which has translations).
